title: Double Diamond: the essential role of the UX Designer
description: The four stages of the Double Diamond, how Design Thinking complements the process and the tools that support each phase.
updateNote: Update note (2026): some of the tools mentioned have changed or been replaced since this was published. Look at the principle behind each one, not the name.

related.title: Clint Acquire
related.body: In practice: a landing page and a conversational flow that captured 79% of sales demand.

blocks.text: The UX person's role in building digital products goes beyond visual design. They help build practical, innovative solutions, from deeply understanding users' needs to collaborating with cross-functional teams so the final product delivers an impactful experience. The Design Council's Double Diamond and Design Thinking are key to this process, structuring the UX designer's path through every phase of the project.
The Double Diamond and the UX Designer's Role
The Double Diamond gives a clear view of the UX process, splitting it into four main stages that go from discovering the problem to delivering the solution.

blocks.caption: Scroll the page: first we open up the problem and converge on a definition; then we open up solutions and converge on delivery.
Diverge to understand, converge to decide, twice.

blocks.text: 1. Discover (First Diamond):

The discovery phase is where the UX designer gathers information and identifies core problems through qualitative and quantitative research. Data collection uses tools like Google Forms and SurveyMonkey, while organization platforms like Notion and Miro help document and structure insights. The UX role is essential here, since they need to align findings with stakeholder expectations, validating hypotheses with real data.
2. Define:

With the information in hand, the next step is to define the core problem objectively. Collaborative sessions in Miro or FigJam are useful for sharing findings and involving stakeholders, building a shared, focused understanding of the challenge to tackle.
3. Develop (Second Diamond):

This phase focuses on exploring potential solutions to the defined problem. Prototyping and usability testing come into play, with tools like Figma, InVision and Adobe XD, where the UX designer builds interactive prototypes to visualize and test the experience before final development.
4. Deliver:

The last phase includes final adjustments to the product, making sure every decision is aligned with users' needs. Additional tests, reviews and final validations are done to confirm the solution fits. Feedback tools like Zoom are useful for capturing live insights and driving refinements.
Design Thinking in UX Practice
Design Thinking complements the Double Diamond by offering a more iterative, user-centered framework made up of five main stages:

items: Empathize: the UX designer observes and interviews users to capture real needs, using tools like Google Docs to document insights. This stage is crucial for a deep understanding of the experiences and challenges users face.
Define the Problem: synthesizing the information leads to a clear, well-scoped problem definition, making it easier to develop focused solutions aligned with the needs identified.

Ideate: collaborative brainstorming sessions allow exploring several solutions. Here, the UX Designer's role is to guide and facilitate the process, encouraging participation and a diversity of ideas.
Prototype: with Figma and Adobe XD, ideas take shape as prototypes, where the team can visualize and iterate on the user interaction before the development phase.

Test and Iterate: user feedback is built into the product through usability testing, driving continuous improvement. Tools like Zoom are useful for real-time feedback sessions, and analyzing the results lets you adjust the product until it best meets users' expectations.

blocks.text: Tools and the Impact of UX on the Organization
Combining UX methods and tools results in products that are better aligned with the target audience, optimizing resources and cutting costs. Some tools:

blocks.caption: The tools from this article organized by phase.

blocks.text: Research and Data Collection

items: Google Forms, SurveyMonkey, Typeform: popular tools for collecting quantitative and qualitative data.
Notion Forms: great for custom forms and surveys with a more specific design.

blocks.text: Organization and Collaboration

items: FigJam, Miro, Mural, Notion: collaborative platforms that make it easier to map and organize ideas.

blocks.text: Prototyping

items: Figma, Adobe XD, InVision: leading tools for building interactive, high-fidelity prototypes.
Sketch: a lightweight alternative, popular among interface designers.

blocks.text: Testing and Analysis

items: UserTesting: for running usability tests with real users.
Hotjar and Clarity (Microsoft): offer heatmaps, session recordings and interaction reports.

blocks.text: A well-structured digital product with a focus on UX provides a positive experience and boosts market competitiveness, creating more user satisfaction and driving engagement.
Conclusion

The UX Designer's role in building digital products is vital to make sure the final product not only meets users' expectations but also offers an engaging, intuitive experience. By applying methods like the Double Diamond and Design Thinking, the UX Designer acts as a bridge between users' needs and innovative solutions, contributing directly to the product's success.

For more information and case studies on the impact of UX, check out UXDesign.cc and the Interaction Design Foundation, as well as the article “Double Diamond and the role of the UX Designer” from the Nielsen Norman Group.
